描述_EN: A blue-glazed water chestnut-type three-system vase，Qing Yongzheng, reign name of Qing emperor (1722-1735)，your (honorific)14.6centimetre，caliber7centimetre，footsteps11.1centimetre。　　bottle apron，short-necked，sloping shoulder，There are three systems in the shoulder，lit. have a large flat abdomen，scholar。Green glaze on the whole body and inside the foot。Raised two strings on the abdomen，Convex lotus petal pattern for one week near the base。Blue and white on the inside of the foot“大Qing Yongzheng, reign name of Qing emperor (1722-1735)年制”Three lines and six characters in seal script。　　Green glaze is the oldest color glaze in China.，至Qing Yongzheng, reign name of Qing emperor (1722-1735)时，景德镇青釉瓷器的生产达到了烧瓷史上的最your (honorific)峰。The green glazes at this time include bean green、holly、pale blue、plum blossom、Crab shell green variety。Yongzheng period green glaze with a glossy surface、robust and fine textured、fine (texture)，This feature was maintained until the Qianlong、Jiaqing period (1796-1820), reign name of Qing emperor (1796-1820)。　　Water chestnut style bottle is a popular porcelain bottle style in the Qing Dynasty，First created in the Kangxi period。Its straight neck is thicker，There is a difference between a flared mouth and a straight mouth，The bellies of the vessels are all flat and rounded，Eleocharis dulcis or Eleocharis dulcis (Chinese water chestnut)，hence the name，Also known as straight-necked bottles。Varieties include blue and white、Yellow glazed blue and white、Bean green glaze、Langyao Red, etc.。
描述_ZN: Green velvet silver and gold-plated stone hoop with inlaid beads, Qing dynasty, Jiaqing, 25 cm long, 3-7.5 cm wide. Qing Palace old collection.    This headband was worn under the inlay when the empress was in auspicious dress, and could play a role in hair appointment and decoration. With a yellow paper label with ink writing on it: "Received on the fifteenth day of the tenth month of the sixth year of the Jiaqing period, presented by the Jingsi room, six pieces of silver and gold-plated flower rests and five pieces of glass flower rests with eleven embedded false beads."
